page: UpCloud PREMIUM-80xCPU-512GB is a high-density, multi-core cloud instance within the Premium server family. It is powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9575F processor, delivering 80 physical cores and 80 vCPUs at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz on a shared allocation model under KVM virtualization. The processor integrates 64 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache, complemented by advanced instruction support including AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic extensions such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The server is configured with 512 GB of system memory (6.4 GB per vCPU) and includes 500 GB of local SSD storage along with one complimentary public IPv4 address. No dedicated hardware GPUs are attached.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional raw compute and parallel throughput. In stress-ng, the system scores 3,021.58 on single-core and 173,282.24 on multi-core execution, placing multi-core scaling in the top 10 percent. Geekbench results echo this pattern with a single-core score of 2,595.0, a multi-core score of 24,610.0, and a software compilation score of 60,936.0 using Clang. PassMark confirms top-tier performance with an overall CPU score of 109,497.78 and extended instruction test score of 130,235.91. Memory bandwidth tests yield 9,301.72 GB/sec for cached 16 KB read blocks and 262.5 GB/sec for large 256 MB uncached reads, while compression tasks show single-threaded gzip throughput of 39.97 GB/sec and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaching 813.68 GB/sec.

Data handling and operational metrics show significant strengths alongside architectural boundaries. Redis SET operations reach 124.66 million operations per second, ranking in the top 10 percent, while database operations score 30,779.71 and static web serving delivers 76.16 GB/sec. Conversely, CPU-bound machine learning tasks reveal clear tradeoffs: while small (135M) model prompt processing achieves 1,140.08 tokens per second, token generation throughput falls to 46.51 tokens per second on the 135M model and 7.85 tokens per second on a 7B model, reflecting the absence of dedicated accelerators. The configuration provides strong computational density per core for parallelized compilation, in-memory caching, multi-threaded backend services, and high-concurrency batch processing.
description: UpCloud PREMIUM-80xCPU-512GB is a high-capacity compute instance powered by an 80-core AMD EPYC 9575F processor at 2.0 GHz, running on KVM virtualization across an x86_64 architecture with shared CPU allocation. It is equipped with 512 GB of RAM (6.4 GB per vCPU), 500 GB of bundled local SSD storage, and one public IPv4 address, without GPU acceleration. CPU benchmarks place this instance in the top 10 percent for multi-core performance, achieving a PassMark CPU score of 109,497.78 and Geekbench multi-core score of 24,610.0. Memory subsystems deliver high cached bandwidth, while operational tests show 124.66 million Redis SET operations per second and 76.16 GB/sec web throughput. Although CPU-based LLM token generation is constrained, the massive core count and substantial memory footprint make it well positioned for large-scale code compilation, distributed caching, parallel simulations, and intensive database workloads.
